Curlimp 0.3.1 updates the native engine and fixes cookie isolation, automatic Referer handling, and incremental native builds. The 39 profiles, default Chrome 150 profile, and command-line scope are unchanged.

## Security and fixes

- Update patched libcurl from 8.22.0 to 8.23.0, incorporating upstream security fixes, including [CVE-2026-92392](https://curl.se/docs/CVE-2026-92392.html) in HTTP/2 uploads. This release does not claim an exploit was demonstrated against Curlimp.
- Enable libpsl 0.23.3 and its pinned built-in Public Suffix List. Response cookies scoped to public or private suffixes are rejected; valid parent-domain cookies remain supported.
- Support `-e ';auto'` and `--referer 'URL;auto'` when following redirects. The last Referer option wins.
- Rebuild the C bridge and relink when native headers, libraries, or provenance change at an unchanged installation path.
- Cache native CI builds while rerunning runtime checks, and gate website deployment on matching published artifacts.

## Update or try Docker

```sh
docker pull juanfontes/curlimp:latest
docker run --rm juanfontes/curlimp:0.3.1 -sS -I https://httpbin.org/status/200
docker run --rm juanfontes/curlimp:0.3.1 firefox147 --json-output -sS -i https://httpbin.org/status/418
```

`latest` follows stable releases, but Docker may reuse your cached image until you pull it. Pin `0.3.1` or the digest below for fixed deployments. Both Linux amd64 and arm64 are available.

## Native downloads and verification

Download the matching Linux amd64/arm64 or experimental macOS Apple Silicon archive and `SHA256SUMS`. Verify the checksum, extract the archive, and keep the entire bundle together. Run `./curlimp --version` to inspect both CLI and engine versions. The packages include runtime dependencies, their notices, provenance, and Zsh profile completion.

On Linux, use `sha256sum --check SHA256SUMS --ignore-missing`. On macOS, select the matching archive line and pass it to `shasum -a 256 --check`. See the [installation guide](https://juanfontes.github.io/curlimp/docs/installation/) for complete commands.

## Validation and scope

Regression checks cover automatic Referer behavior, public/private/internationalized suffix cookies, valid domain exceptions, and native dependency rebuilds. Release builds also check HTTP/TLS/HTTP2, all profile selections, response exports, certificates, completion, native packaging, and the minimal Linux runtime.

One HTTP(S) URL per invocation; a documented subset of curl options. No browser rendering or JavaScript execution. Real-browser fingerprint equivalence and HTTP/3 end-to-end behavior remain unverified. macOS packages are signed ad hoc, not notarized; Windows and Intel Mac native packages are not provided.
